newsitem.title: USA: Vereinsbank opposes unconditioned TARGET access.
newsitem.headline: Vereinsbank opposes unconditioned TARGET access.

text.p: Germany's Bayerische Vereinsbank AG said Sunday it was opposed to Britain being given access to the TARGET payment system for the planned European currency unless it shared in the responsibilities created by the currency.

The bank's chief executive Albrecht Schmidt said in a sppech delivered in Washington on Saturday evening that London would gain an advantage over continental European financial centres if it was allowed to participate in TARGET without joining the European currency.
The system will channel central bank payment systems in the new European currency, the Euro, after its creation in 1999 when European Economic and Monetary Union starts.
It will also give banks access to interest-free intra-day credits, necessary if banks are to be able to offer a full range of transactions denominated in Euro.

Concern that the Bank of England may be excluded from the TARGET system if Britain decides not to join the Euro in the first round has placed a question mark over the role of London as a financial centre after the start of EMU.

But some banks on the continent, seeing the opportunity to attract Euro business to local financial centres, have argued it would be unfair for London to gain the benefits of the Euro payment system without having to comply with the rules of monetary union.
"We are strictly against privileges for London which are not accompanied by duties as a result of participation in monetary union," Schmidt said.
